hints: Acceleration is the slope of the v–t graph. What are the slopes of AM and MB?
worded:
1. AM is a straight line going down: constant negative slope, so a constant negative acceleration.

2. MB is a straight line going up: constant positive acceleration.

3. So a is a negative constant, then jumps to a positive constant at M, and stays there. (B)

4. (A) keeps switching sign, (C) is smooth, and (D) is never negative: all out.
conventional:
![](asset:P000167-sol-1)

$$a_{AM} = slope\ of\ AM < 0\ (constant),\quad\quad a_{MB} = slope\ of\ MB > 0\ (constant).$$

The a–t graph is a step from a negative value to a positive value at the instant of M: graph (B).
mistakes: The sign of a follows the slope of v, not the sign of v: velocity is negative near M but the acceleration there is positive on the MB side.
